clue.text: Discerning of poet to stand by earliest of comments quoted on the radio

indicators.note: what is heard on the radio is only sound, so the words are judged by how they are spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: John Clare is the poet; 'of poet' is the possessive

parts.words: to stand by earliest of comments quoted
parts.note: cited means quoted or called in to stand by a claim, and it opens with the first letter of comments

explanation.surface: A poet with good judgement stands by the first remarks he made in a radio interview.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken aloud, 'Clare's cited' becomes CLEAR-SIGHTED; the wordplay is loose, with 'earliest of comments' only pointing to the C that starts the second sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone clear-sighted sees situations accurately and judges them well, an exact synonym of being discerning.

clue.text: Dismiss more reserved account put up earlier

indicators.note: in a down entry, putting something up means writing it from bottom to top

parts.note: AC is the standard abbreviation for account
comparative of shy

explanation.surface: A bank threatens to dismiss a client whose account is more cautious than before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Earlier' places the reversed abbreviation in front of the comparative.
explanation.definitionFit: To cashier an officer is to dismiss them from the armed forces in disgrace.

clue.text: Hurt after I said something very ugly

indicators.note: coming after means following, so the word before it in the clue is placed second
what is said is heard, not written, so the single letter stands for a word sounding the same

parts.note: the letter I sounds like the organ of sight
hurt as an adjective: painful

explanation.surface: Someone is wounded after making a cruel remark.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyesore is an ugly sight, typically a building that spoils its surroundings.

clue.text: Showing signs of anger old soul singer describes being regularly disregarded

indicators.note: to describe in geometry is to draw a line around, so the singer encloses the other letters

parts.note: Otis Redding, the 1960s soul singer

indicators.note: every other letter of the word is ignored, leaving the evenly spaced remainder

parts.note: the second and fourth letters of being

explanation.surface: An old soul singer gets angry describing how he was ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Going red in the face is the classic sign of mounting anger.

clue.text: Run into dog close to home

parts.note: being in means being at home
a cur is a mongrel

explanation.surface: A dog runs into someone near its house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close to' just sets the two pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: To incur debts or a penalty is to run into them, to bring them upon yourself.

clue.text: Opposed by those resolved to protect the borders of Israel

indicators.note: protecting something means surrounding it, so the rearranged letters enclose the edges
resolved can mean broken down and recombined, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

indicators.note: the borders of a word are its outer edges, its first and last letters

parts.note: first and last letters of Israel

explanation.surface: A politician is opposed by people determined to defend Israel's frontiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Hostile means antagonistic, so being opposed to something is being hostile to it.

clue.text: Survive on the way up by the ability to recognise a harmful glance

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the word is written from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to live is to survive
having an eye for something is a knack for spotting it

explanation.surface: A survivor climbing upward shows a talent for spotting a malicious look.
explanation.definitionFit: The evil eye is a look superstitiously believed to cause harm or bad luck to its target.

clue.text: Dead against new nurses beginning to vouch for an unfavourable state of affairs

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold close, so the rearranged letters cradle the single letter
something new has been remade, so these letters take a fresh order

parts.note: both words taken as written, to be rearranged

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter only

parts.note: first letter of vouch

explanation.surface: Nurses firmly opposed to a new policy speak up for a poor situation.
explanation.definitionFit: A disadvantage is an unfavourable condition or circumstance that hampers success.

clue.text: It's Dean playing as a substitute

indicators.note: players move around a pitch, so the letters shift into new positions

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A footballer called Dean comes on as a replacement player.
explanation.definitionFit: Instead means in place of something else, which is how a substitute stands in.

clue.text: Happen to miss bit of practice before batting in county game

indicators.note: the earlier pieces are put inside the abbreviation that follows

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for county

indicators.note: missing something means going without it, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: as in 'come to pass'

indicators.note: only a small piece, the first letter, of the following word is taken

parts.note: first letter of practice
the side batting in cricket is in

explanation.surface: A county cricketer skips some practice before going in to bat.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket setting hides the card game: 'happen' here is the sense in 'come to pass', and 'batting' gives the cricketer's word for being at the crease.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassino is a card game in which players capture cards from the table by matching values.

clue.text: Extended period of imprisonment received by debarred journalist

indicators.note: what is received is taken inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: shut out, excluded
a stretch is slang for a prison sentence
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: A disgraced journalist is handed a lengthy jail sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: Outstretched describes arms or limbs reached out to full length, so it means extended.

clue.text: Points to a ring around sink resembling fat

indicators.note: going around something means enclosing it, so the article and the ring sit either side

parts.note: taken as written
to dip is to sink a little
O is ring-shaped
two compass points, south and east

explanation.surface: Someone points out a ring of grime around the kitchen sink that looks greasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Points to' puts the compass letters after the rest, even though they lead the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Adipose tissue is the body's fatty tissue, so the adjective means fatty or of fat.

clue.text: Intend to put on torn clothing

indicators.note: clothes that are put on surround the wearer, so one word wears the other

parts.note: rent is an old word for torn, as in a rent garment
to aim to do something is to intend it

explanation.surface: Someone plans to wear ripped clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put on' suits the clothing surface, but here it means one word goes inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiment is a literary or archaic word for garments and attire.

clue.text: Vulnerable at the outset before crossing German border

indicators.note: the outset is the start, so only the opening letter counts

parts.note: first letter of vulnerable

indicators.note: the word lies across the abbreviation, enclosing it

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
G is the abbreviation for German

explanation.surface: Someone exposed and at risk is about to cross the German frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before' looks like a positional link but supplies ERE, which then holds G.
explanation.definitionFit: A verge is an edge or margin, such as the grass strip bordering a road.

clue.text: Constituent initially ignored by Independent politician's agent

indicators.note: the initial letter is ignored, so the word loses its first letter

parts.note: I is the abbreviation for Independent
MP is a Member of Parliament
an element is a component part

explanation.surface: A voter is snubbed by an independent MP's representative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Constituent' suggests a voter in an MP's seat, but here it means a component.
explanation.definitionFit: An implement is a tool, and an agent can mean the means or instrument by which something is done.

clue.text: Freedom from restraint shown by Penny's trite remark

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for penny
latitude is freedom of action

explanation.surface: Penny's casual dismissal of freedom is a hackneyed observation.
explanation.definitionFit: A platitude is a dull, overused statement offered as if it were meaningful.

clue.text: False allegations the French dismissed as homesickness

indicators.note: false things are not genuine, so the letters are made up into something else
what is dismissed is sent away, so those letters are removed

parts.note: taken as written
le is French for the

explanation.surface: French officials brushed off untrue accusations as mere homesickness.
explanation.definitionFit: Nostalgia originally meant acute longing for home, and the word still carries that sense.

clue.text: Kind of dog bed found in street on the outskirts of Ilfracombe

indicators.note: something found in a place lies within it, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street
a cot is a small bed

indicators.note: the outskirts of a word are its edges, the first and last letters

parts.note: first and last letters of Ilfracombe

explanation.surface: A dog's bed turns up in a street on the edge of a Devon seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: Ilfracombe is a resort on the north coast of Devon in England.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottie is a Scottish terrier, a breed of small wiry-coated dog.

clue.text: Vehicle originally departing from Parisian company's design style

indicators.note: the original, first letter departs, so the word loses its opening

parts.note: a cart is a simple vehicle
de is French for of or from
CO is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A car leaving a Paris firm shows off the company's styling.
explanation.definitionFit: Art Deco is the bold geometric decorative style of the 1920s and 1930s.

clue.text: Quiet for a gun they say

indicators.note: what people say is spoken, so the word is matched by its sound alone

parts.note: piece is slang for a gun

explanation.surface: Someone asks for silence in exchange for a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: Piece is American slang for a handgun.
explanation.definitionFit: Peace means calm and quiet, freedom from noise or disturbance.

clue.text: Head of planning apt to be easily influenced

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of planning
apt to and liable to both mean likely to

explanation.surface: The head of the planning department is prone to being swayed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone pliable bends easily to others' wishes, as a pliable material bends.

clue.text: Draw close to elephant in the heart of uncharted territory

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its last letter is taken

parts.note: middle letter of uncharted

indicators.note: the single letter is placed inside the following pieces

parts.note: a tract is an area of land

indicators.note: the heart is the centre, so only the middle letter is wanted

parts.note: last letter of elephant

explanation.surface: An explorer draws near an elephant deep in unmapped land.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw a crowd is to attract it, pulling people in.

clue.text: Pioneering advocate for a permanent military establishment near the centre of Hartlepool

parts.note: taken as written
a military post is a fixed station

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle pair of letters

parts.note: middle two letters of Hartlepool

explanation.surface: A campaigner calls for a permanent army base close to the middle of Hartlepool.
explanation.walkthrough: Hartlepool is a port town in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostle is a leading early champion of a cause, after the first followers who spread Christianity.

clue.text: Just before time of incident

parts.note: even as in just, fair
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A note just before the time something happened.
explanation.definitionFit: An event is something that happens, an occurrence, the same as an incident.

clue.text: Senseless to get beginners in immunology doing investigations of the ear

indicators.note: beginners are the first letters of each of the next three words

parts.note: first letters of immunology, doing and investigations
otic is the anatomical adjective for the ear

explanation.surface: Students new to immunology are pointlessly probing ears.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiotic means foolish or stupid, lacking good sense.

clue.text: Not usual in America to leave additional space at end of page

indicators.note: the abbreviation goes out of the word, so its letter is dropped

parts.note: extra means additional
an em is a printer's unit of space

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

parts.note: last letter of page
A is the abbreviation for America

explanation.surface: An American publisher unusually leaves extra space at the foot of a page.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In America' suggests US usage, but America just provides the letter A to be removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Extreme means far beyond the ordinary, so it describes something not usual.

clue.text: Resentment evident in letter about the source of Brexit madness

indicators.note: turned about means facing the other way, so the letter is written back to front

parts.note: mu is a Greek letter

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it starts, its first letter

parts.note: first letter of Brexit
rage is fury, a kind of madness

explanation.surface: Bitterness shows in a letter written about the folly of Brexit.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking umbrage means taking offence, a feeling of resentment at a slight.

clue.text: Unworthy of goddess left in race when disregarding the rules

indicators.note: the goddess and the letter are placed inside the race

parts.note: below as in beneath one's dignity
the TT is the Isle of Man motorbike race
Hebe is the Greek goddess of youth
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A goddess abandoning a race in a fit of rule-breaking falls short of her divine standing.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT (Tourist Trophy) is a famous motorcycle race on the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: From boxing, where hitting under the waistband is illegal, the idiom means unfair or against the rules.
